note: Rules auditor for D1 stage B (P25): turns recorded traces into mutation proposals. Each rule names the trace event, the pattern (grouping keys + min count), the proposed mutation (M5.3 vocabulary) and the target. The auditor only proposes (updates/traces-proposals.jsonl + TRACE-EVOLUTION.md) - never touches data|core|domains|templates (M0.4/M0.8). Patterns come from the D1 design doc §3; the low-outcome rule is the P24 effect axis feeding back. 'score_max' rules fire only on numeric scores; grade strings are human territory. P45.R1: task_outcome receipts may declare detail.scale ([lo, hi]); scaled receipts are compared by normalized score (low_max_normalized), unscaled ones keep the legacy raw score_max check.

rules.why: The same gate failing across three or more projects is a fact about the gate's clause, not about the projects: its executable form is missing or wrong (M3 checklist).

A capability that is matched but never referenced across three projects either has no operational surface (Archive) or a mis-set trigger (then Deepen instead); both are registry defects (M5.3 vocabulary).

rules.target: default parameters or domain signals for the task family
rules.why: The same task family being re-derived means the first selection was insufficient twice; the default the engine picked for that family is the thing to change.
A human correction is the strongest signal the loop has; two corrections concentrated on one capability mean its operating manual has a hole.

rules.target: the harness of the task family named by detail.task
rules.why: P24's effect axis feeding back: two measured low outcomes on the same task family is evidence the emitted harness does not achieve its effect, not just that its structure is wrong. P45.R1: receipts that declare detail.scale ([lo, hi]) are compared by their NORMALIZED score (low_max_normalized); scale-less receipts fall back to the raw score_max check - a known ambiguity, so declaring the scale is the fix (an M3.19 outcome-validity point on the effect axis itself).
